purpose: Reveal the two predeclared validation velocity and dispersion fields and compare them with fixed Newtonian and MOND predictions from both real registered baryons and velocity-blind Haar-256 synthetic twins.

parents.failedTwinDisclosure: The frozen Haar-256 validation twin failed the NGC6946 gas-map and median line-of-sight transport gates. P0746 scores it unchanged so the source-map formula result and the twin degradation remain separately visible.

observationProcessing.method: Unchanged P0744 observation and scoring implementation generalized only to the validation split and frozen parent paths.
observationProcessing.skyCenter: fixed SPARC/NED coordinate already used for baryonic registration
observationProcessing.systemicVelocity: one disclosed H I-intensity-weighted central median observation nuisance per galaxy
observationProcessing.handedness: one disclosed binary observation-coordinate convention per galaxy
observationProcessing.scoreMask: finite moment 0, moment 1, and moment 2 samples with positive gas weight from one beam to H I R995
observationProcessing.uncertaintyKmS: quadrature sum of moment-2 dispersion and universal 5.2 km/s channel FWHM divided by 2.355
observationProcessing.predictionBeam: THINGS geometric-mean circular Gaussian with gas-intensity weighting

interpretation.fieldErrorRatio: gas-weighted prediction RMSE divided by gas-weighted RMS measurement-plus-dispersion uncertainty
interpretation.warning: Bands are descriptive. A validation result is not a holdout result, and the raw circular model omits known non-circular gas dynamics.

claimBoundary: P0746 is the first unchanged-method validation-split 2D velocity-field comparison for the spiral twins; it is not the final holdout.
The formula scores on registered baryons answer whether the fixed law predicts the real field; twin scores additionally test the simulator reconstruction.
The frozen Haar-256 twin is retained despite its disclosed NGC6946 validation morphology failure, preventing validation-driven retuning before target reveal.
No pressure support, warp, bar, streaming, inclination, distance, M/L, MOND, or halo parameter is fitted to the revealed residuals.
A miss can mix gravity-law error with omitted gas dynamics, so source-versus-twin transport and spatial residual structure must be reported separately.
Both holdout galaxies and all their pixel arrays remain sealed.
